title: Conditional Kunneth formula for oriented nearby cycles
statement:
Let $B$ be a scheme and $f_i:T_i\to B$ finite-type morphisms [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] for $i=1,2$. Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring annihilated by an integer $m\geq1$ invertible on $B$. Let $L_i\in D^b(T_{i,\mathrm{Et}},\Lambda)$, and assume that both $(f_i,L_i)$ are $\Psi$-good [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles]. Put $T=T_1\times_BT_2$, $f:T\to B$, $q_i:T\to T_i$ and $v_i:V_f\to V_{f_i}$ as in that definition. Then the specified oriented Kunneth comparison
$$v_1^*R\Psi_{f_1}L_1\otimes_\Lambda^Lv_2^*R\Psi_{f_2}L_2\longrightarrow R\Psi_f(q_1^*L_1\otimes_\Lambda^Lq_2^*L_2)$$
is an isomorphism in $D(V_f,\Lambda)$. This is a conditional assertion about total-scheme complexes and vanishing topoi over an arbitrary base; it makes no assertion that a given pair is $\Psi$-good.

source.place: Theorem A.3(1) with Y_1=Y_2=B, pp. 2--3, and the torsion finite-type sufficient condition for (*) preceding Remark A.2, p. 1; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Each $f_i$ is locally of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and $\Lambda$ is torsion because $m\Lambda=0$. Thus [lem-trf-finite-type-torsion-universal-star] supplies condition (*) universally for both $f_i$. It also applies to $f:T_1\times_BT_2\to B$: on affine charts finite-type algebras $A[u_1,\ldots,u_r]/I$ and $A[v_1,\ldots,v_s]/J$ have tensor product $A[u_1,\ldots,u_r,v_1,\ldots,v_s]/(I,J)$, so $f$ is locally of finite type. The input complexes are bounded, hence in $D^-$. The tensor product of the two inputs need not be bounded below; the universal (*) hypotheses allow the unbounded local description used next.

source.place: Definition A.1 and Remark A.2, pp. 1--2; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text:
Fix a geometric point $x$ of $T$, and denote its images in $T_i$ and $B$ by $x_i$ and $b$. Put $S=B_{(b)}$, $X_i=(T_i)_{(x_i)}$, $X=T_{(x)}$, $g_i:X_i\to S$, $a:X\to X_1$, $d:X\to X_2$, and $g=g_1a=g_2d$. Write $A=L_1|_{X_1}$ and $C=L_2|_{X_2}$. Here $X$ is the strict localization at $x$ of $X_1\times_SX_2$, not the whole fibre product. By [lem-trf-oriented-nearby-strict-local-description], it suffices to show that the canonical local map
$$c_x:Rg_{1*}A\otimes_\Lambda^LRg_{2*}C\longrightarrow Rg_*(a^*A\otimes_\Lambda^Ld^*C)$$
is an isomorphism for every $x$. The node identifies precisely this map with the restriction of the comparison specified by [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles], including its ordinary-comparison and lax-tensor components.

source.place: Proof of Theorem A.3, pp. 2--3; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text:
The two goodness hypotheses and [lem-trf-oriented-nearby-strict-local-description] give localized base-change invariance for $(g_1,A)$ and $(g_2,C)$. Applying the latter to the essentially Cartesian square with top map $d:X\to X_2$ and bottom map $g_1:X_1\to S$ gives
$$e:g_1^*Rg_{2*}C\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_*d^*C.$$
The same node gives localized base-change invariance for $(a,d^*C)$. Indeed, $a$ is the strict localization of the base change of $f_2$ to $X_1$, and pasting another essentially Cartesian square gives a localized base change of $(g_2,C)$. All three direct images $g_1,g_2,a$ have finite cohomological dimension by [lem-trf-finite-type-torsion-universal-star]. Since $C$ is bounded, $Rg_{2*}C\in D^-$: if $\mathcal H^q(C)=0$ for $q>r$ and the cohomological-dimension bound is $N$, the finite truncation filtration of $C$ has pieces $\mathcal H^q(C)[-q]$, whose direct images vanish above $q+N$, so $Rg_{2*}C$ vanishes above $r+N$. Also $A$ and $d^*C$ are bounded, because inverse image on constant-coefficient modules is exact.

source.place: Proof of Theorem A.3, pp. 2--3; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-trf-strict-local-base-invariant-projection] first to $(g_1,A,M=Rg_{2*}C)$ and then to $(a,d^*C,M=A)$. The bounds and localized base-change invariance were checked in step 3. The composite
$$\begin{aligned}
Rg_{1*}A\otimes^LRg_{2*}C
&\xrightarrow{\mathrm{PF}_{g_1}}Rg_{1*}(A\otimes^Lg_1^*Rg_{2*}C)\\
&\xrightarrow{Rg_{1*}(1\otimes e)}Rg_{1*}(A\otimes^LRa_*d^*C)\\
&\xrightarrow{Rg_{1*}(\mathrm{PF}_a)}Rg_{1*}Ra_*(a^*A\otimes^Ld^*C)\\
&\simeq Rg_*(a^*A\otimes^Ld^*C)
\end{aligned}$$
is an isomorphism. In the third arrow the tensor symmetries put $d^*C$ in the direct-image slot of the projection formula. The last identification uses the composite adjunction $g^*=a^*g_1^*\dashv Rg_{1*}Ra_*$: composing the two Hom adjunction bijections shows this is the right adjoint of $g^*$, and hence identifies it canonically with $Rg_*$.

source.place: Proof of Theorem A.3, pp. 2--3; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text:
This composite is $c_x$, not merely an unspecified isomorphism between its source and target. Under $g^*\dashv Rg_*$ its adjunct is
$$a^*g_1^*Rg_{1*}A\otimes^Ld^*g_2^*Rg_{2*}C\xrightarrow{a^*\varepsilon_{g_1,A}\otimes d^*\varepsilon_{g_2,C}}a^*A\otimes^Ld^*C.$$
To check it, expand each projection morphism as the adjoint of counit tensor identity [def-kun-projection-formula-map]. The exchange $e$ is the adjoint of $a^*g_1^*Rg_{2*}C=d^*g_2^*Rg_{2*}C\to d^*C$, so $\varepsilon_a\circ a^*e=d^*\varepsilon_{g_2,C}$. The composite-adjunction counit is $\varepsilon_a\circ a^*\varepsilon_{g_1}$. Substitution leaves exactly the displayed tensor of two counits; the tensor symmetries in step 4 cancel. By [lem-trf-oriented-nearby-strict-local-description] this is also the adjunct defining the restricted oriented comparison. Equality of adjuncts gives equality of maps. Thus all restricted comparisons are isomorphisms, and the joint conservativity in that node proves the original comparison is an isomorphism.
